questions.explain: The key insight is you buy the sum of average utilization plus headroom for coincident peaks, not the sum of peaks — that is what makes pools 60–80% cheaper than individual provisioning.
options: The sum of each database's peak vCores
The total storage of all databases
The sum of average utilization plus headroom for coincident peaks
The peak utilization of the largest tenant
questions.q: How should an elastic pool be sized?

questions.explain: Per-database max caps are the first and most important noisy-neighbor defense — one tenant's runaway query should degrade that tenant, not exhaust the pool.
options: Per-database max caps
Failover groups
Geo-restore
Elastic query
questions.q: What is the first and most important control against noisy neighbors in an elastic pool?

questions.explain: The chapter's comparison: pools win when databases are lightly busy around the clock; serverless wins when they are truly idle for long stretches. Measure idle patterns, then choose.
options: Pools always win for any fleet
Serverless always wins for any fleet
Whichever has the larger min vCores
Pools for lightly-busy-around-the-clock fleets, serverless for truly-idle-for-hours databases
questions.q: Per the chapter, how do you choose between an elastic pool and serverless for a fleet of tenant databases?

questions.explain: For per-tenant recovery, geo-restore works per database — restore a single tenant from geo-redundant backups without touching the rest of the pool; its RPO is up to an hour versus seconds for active geo-replication.
options: A failover group must fail over the whole pool
Geo-restore works per database, without touching the rest of the pool
Per-tenant restore requires splitting the pool first
Single-tenant restores are not supported
questions.q: A single SaaS tenant needs yesterday's data back. How does the chapter recommend handling it?

questions.explain: Do not pool tenants with correlated peaks — the pool must be sized near the sum of peaks, erasing the savings. Also don't pool tenants needing different compliance boundaries or tiers.
options: Tenants with storage over 500 GB
Tenants with uncorrelated peaks
Tenants with correlated peaks (e.g., all B2B customers active 9–5 in one timezone)
Tenants using T-SQL
